subject: Numerical Problems in MCMC Metropolis Simulation

messages.author: 4dea34ee42cd8b1c
messages.subject: Numerical Problems in MCMC Metropolis Simulation
parts:
I keep running RStan with 4 chains and, on two chains every time, the following error message appears:

The following numerical problems occured the indicated number of times after warmup on chain 3
                                                                                            count
validate transformed params: thetahome[k0__] is nan, but must be greater than or equal to 0     1
When a numerical problem occurs, the Metropolis proposal gets rejected.
However, by design Metropolis proposals sometimes get rejected even when there are no numerical problems.
Thus, if the number in the 'count' column is small, do not ask about this message on stan-users.

How can transformed parameters be validated? And what is the count column?

Kind regards,

Tom.

On Monday, May 2, 2016 at 1:37:51 PM UTC-4, Tom Parker wrote:
I keep running RStan with 4 chains and, on two chains every time, the following error message appears:

The following numerical problems occured the indicated number of times after warmup on chain 3
                                                                                            count
validate transformed params: thetahome[k0__] is nan, but must be greater than or equal to 0     1
When a numerical problem occurs, the Metropolis proposal gets rejected.
However, by design Metropolis proposals sometimes get rejected even when there are no numerical problems.
Thus, if the number in the 'count' column is small, do not ask about this message on stan-users.

How can transformed parameters be validated? And what is the count column?

In a fixed-width font, the count column is at the far right. So, you have one transition out of several thousand where one value of thetahome was realized as 0 / 0 or something, and when Stan attempted to validate that it failed, so the proposal was rejected in favor of the realization of the parameters on the previous iteration. But that will make no appreciable difference to your inferences

Ben

messages.author: 8aa9b8cc06fdc99c
messages.subject: Re: [stan-users] Numerical Problems in MCMC Metropolis Simulation
parts:
See the end of the message. To get rid of all these issues,
you can reduce step size and increase target acceptance rate. The
problem is that floating point arithmetic can easily underflow and
overflow, espeically when there are exponentiation operations. But
given this only happened once (that count of 1), it's no big deal,
as the error message tries to indicate.

Transformed parameters are always validated against their declared
constraints.

The message is problematic in that there's no Metropolis rejection
in NUTS (though there is in basic static HMC) --- it's slice sampled.

- Bob

messages.subject: Re: [stan-users] Numerical Problems in MCMC Metropolis Simulation
parts:
It was slice up until the recent update, but they all yield the
same marginal probabilities of selecting each state in a
given trajectory.  In particular, all of these methods exactly
correct for any error in the numerical integrator.
